title: What angle do you get from one more half fold?
description: Half of forty five degrees is found by splitting it into forty and five, which gives twenty two and a half degrees. Keeko's doubt, that half of forty five is twenty three, is broken by putting two such pieces together.
teaching_notes: One idea: half of forty five is twenty plus two and a half. Watch for children who round the half up.

source: Continuing with another half fold as shown in Fig. 2.18, we
video_script.why: The child halves forty five degrees and meets a half degree in the answer.
video_script.substitution: A strip of paper five centimetres long, folded in half, shows that half of an odd number has a half in it.
video_script.anchor: the book's slice of forty five degrees, folded in half once more
video_script.wrong_answer: half of forty five is twenty three
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko rounds half of forty five up to twenty three. Two pieces of twenty three degrees make forty six degrees, one degree too many, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The angle is twenty two point five degrees

final_answer.spoken: the angle is twenty two point five degrees

maths_rules: half of 45 is not 23: 23 + 23 = 46, one too many
video_script.design: The slice stays on the board. The number twenty two point five is written only in the answer beat; the steps show the split of forty five into forty and five.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; the 45° slice folded in half again; the new angle = ____

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears with the slice
marks.fold: the 45° slice is folded in half
marks.ask: a question mark appears over the new slice

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is another half fold from your book about the paper protractor.
<bookmark mark='fold'/>The last slice was forty five degrees. It is folded in half once more.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What angle do we get after this one more half fold?

beats.on_screen: the folded slice stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: a paper strip 5 cm long folded in half; each half is 2.5 cm

marks.strip: a 5 cm strip is folded in half

narration: <bookmark mark='strip'/>Fold a strip of paper five centimetres long in half.
<bookmark mark='half'/>Each half is two and a half centimetres. Half of an odd number is not a whole number.

beats.on_screen: Given: the last angle is 45°; one more fold cuts it in half

marks.given: the line Given is written under the picture

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the last angle is forty five degrees, and one more fold cuts it into two equal angles.

beats.on_screen: To find: the measure of the new angle

marks.find: the line To find is written under the Given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the measure of the new angle.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: the new angle is half of 45°: 45° ÷ 2
narration: <bookmark mark='half'/>Step one, the new angle is half of the old angle of forty five.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: split 45° into 40° and 5°; half of 40° is 20°, half of 5° is 2.5°

marks.halves: 20° and 2.5° are written under the two parts

narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step two, split forty five into forty and five.
<bookmark mark='halves'/>Half of forty is twenty, and half of five is two and a half.

marks.add: the two halves are joined and 20° + 2.5° is written

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step three, add the two halves together, which are twenty and two and a half.

marks.check: two new angles are placed side by side
marks.sum: 20° + 20° + 2.5° + 2.5° = 45° is written and matches the old slice

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check by putting two new angles together.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Twenty twice makes forty, and two and a half twice makes five. Together they make forty five, the old angle.

marks.ans: 22.5° is boxed beside the new slice

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The angle is twenty two point five degrees.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the new slice
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's doubt: half of 45 is 23; two pieces of 23° make 46°, one degree too many; the doubt is crossed out

marks.many: two pieces of 23° are placed on the 45° slice and overflow by 1°
marks.exact: two pieces of 22.5° fit the 45° slice exactly, and the doubt is crossed out

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko says half of forty five is twenty three.
<bookmark mark='many'/>Twenty three and twenty three make forty six, which is one too many.
<bookmark mark='exact'/>Half of forty five is twenty two and a half. Two of those make exactly forty five.
